title: Nvidia CEO Says He Would Cut Off Customers Who Build Unsafe AI
source_used: The Business Times (Singapore), carrying Bloomberg's text; Startup Fortune commentary
key_facts: Jensen Huang, Nvidia chief executive, was interviewed by Bloomberg's Emily Chang in London.
Asked if he would stop supplying an irresponsible AI developer, he said "It's a hypothetical, but yes."
He said a conversation would come first; Nvidia does not run other companies and its technology is general-purpose.
He said fears about AI safety are growing pains and the software can be controlled and deployed safely.
Nvidia is donating US$250 million over five years, as computing time, to UK safety research at institutions including Oxford and University College London.
He named no company and defined no trigger for cutting anyone off (Startup Fortune).
quote_evidence: "It's a hypothetical, but yes," he said in an interview with Bloomberg's Emily Chang in London when asked if he would stop supplying an irresponsible developer.
"We don't run other people's companies, and there's a limit to the judgment we apply to other companies' use of our technology."
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how much leverage the dominant chip supplier could claim over AI developers, with Huang's own hedges attached.
